clue.text: Where to get a Scots rash?

definitions.note: a question asking for a place, which the answer as a Highland district supplies

indicators.note: to get here means to obtain by working the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled traveller asks where in Scotland one might pick up an itchy skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint, but with 'Scots' it is the anagram fodder; 'get' signals the rearrangement, and the result is a wooded glen district of central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trossachs are a scenic region of the Scottish Highlands, so they are a place, answering 'where'.

clue.text: They go up and down the Strand

definitions.text: They go up and down the Strand

parts.words: They go up and down the Strand
parts.note: strand is the shore, and what rises and falls along a shore twice a day is the sea's movement

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Strand' suggests the London street, but here a strand is a beach, where the sea comes in and goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's regular rise and fall moves the waterline up and down every beach.

clue.text: One thing one is not conscious of being

definitions.text: One thing one is not conscious of being

parts.words: One thing one is not conscious of being
parts.note: a state of unawareness that, by its nature, a person cannot notice in themselves

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a riddle about self-knowledge: if you are unaware, you cannot be aware of that unawareness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware of one's surroundings is precisely not to be conscious of them, so one cannot notice being so.

clue.text: Spring in foreign country

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a mineral spring, a SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation abroad for the British setter and solver.

clue.text: A cynic apt to take command

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and rebuilt, so to take them signals that the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptical person who is likely to seize leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue repeated 3-down; the page prints 'A cynic apt to take command'. The letters of A CYNIC APT rearrange, signalled by 'to take', to give the office of a captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Captaincy is the post of leading a team or ship, so it is a position of command.

clue.text: Guys who know when to stop?

definitions.text: Guys who know when to stop?

parts.words: Guys who know when to stop?
parts.note: guys are ropes steadying a mast, and the word for those ropes also means remains or halts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like men, but guys are ropes bracing a mast; their other name also says 'remains', as of a guest who knows when to stop going.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes bracing a mast are its guys, and a person who remains put has stopped moving.

clue.text: The sycophant's progress

parts.note: a flatterer advances by grovelling, moving forward on hands and knees in a slow abject way

explanation.walkthrough: A sycophant is said to grovel; the word for that also means moving slowly on all fours.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadying is described as grovelling, and moving on hands and knees is the slowest kind of progress.

clue.text: This way for the tower

parts.note: a tower here is one who tows a barge, walking the towpath beside the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' suggests a tall building, but it is one who tows: a horse or person pulling a barge walks the path beside the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Barges were hauled by horses walking a towpath along the waterway's edge.

clue.text: If you want friendship, it is found in a girl

indicators.note: one piece is found inside another, so these words place the word it within the girl's name

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Advice that companionship can be found by seeking out a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes inside AMY, a girl's name, as 'is found in' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations or goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Safe things to have on hand

definitions.text: Safe things to have on hand

parts.words: Safe things to have on hand
parts.note: ropes thrown to keep people safe, and also the creases on a palm that a palm-reader inspects

explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' means available, but palmists read lines on the hand, one of which foretells a long existence; rescue ropes are the safe things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue rope keeps a person safe, and palmistry names one crease of the palm after the length of one's days.

clue.text: This girl's back was bad

indicators.note: reading back means the letters for was bad are taken from right to left

parts.note: ailed means was ill, was in bad health

explanation.surface: A girl had a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the girl's body, but it turns AILED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a girl's name, and the clue's 's is 'is', so 'This girl is' leads to the name.

clue.text: It's an obvious quarrel that brings him into action

definitions.note: the man the action is brought by, a pronoun standing for a person

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A clear-cut row is what lands a man in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: An action is a lawsuit; the person who brings one is the 'him' the clue defines, and a quarrel is what drives him to sue.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who starts a civil lawsuit is the one bringing the action against another.

clue.text: How many trees in the Garden of England ?

definitions.text: How many trees in the Garden of England ?

parts.words: How many trees in the Garden of England ?
parts.note: the Garden of England is Kent, and a Kent town is named for a count of oak trees

explanation.walkthrough: The Garden of England is a nickname for Kent, a county of orchards in south-east England; one of its towns has a name that answers 'how many trees' with a number and a kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevenoaks is a town in Kent whose name counts a group of oak trees.

clue.text: Such ties bind a man to Queen and Country

definitions.text: Such ties bind a man to Queen and Country

parts.words: Such ties bind a man to Queen and Country
parts.note: the bonds of faithful allegiance a subject feels to monarch and nation

explanation.walkthrough: 'ties' can suggest neckties, but these are bonds of faithfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful allegiance to sovereign and nation is the bond of a devoted subject.

clue.text: They expect a fair profit

parts.note: fair is a funfair, and those running its rides and stalls hope to make money there

explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like 'reasonable', but it is a funfair; those running its attractions expect to profit from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Showmen run fairground rides and stalls as their trade and make their living from fairs.

clue.text: Likeness points to a doctor with a weapon

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
a lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight

explanation.surface: A portrait shows a physician holding a spear and pointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' gives two compass points, S and E; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward resemblance or appearance of something.

clue.text: Did my grateful patient pay " on the nail " ?

definitions.text: Did my grateful patient pay " on the nail " ?

parts.words: Did my grateful patient pay " on the nail " ?
parts.note: the patient is a man the speaker cured, and the treatment on the nail is a beauty treatment for fingernails

explanation.walkthrough: 'pay on the nail' means pay promptly, but read as a man I cured, the patient's nails were treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands given a nail treatment have had their nails trimmed and shaped.

clue.text: The act of a hedger ?

parts.note: a hedger is one who dodges a question, not a gardener trimming a hedge

explanation.walkthrough: A hedger suggests someone trimming hedges, but to hedge is also to avoid committing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging a straight answer is what someone who hedges does.

clue.text: A look-out man

parts.note: not a sentry but a person whose attention is directed outward to others

explanation.walkthrough: A look-out is a sentry, but read as 'looks out', it is a person turned toward others.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person directs attention outward rather than inward.

clue.text: One naturally interested in local affairs

definitions.text: One naturally interested in local affairs

parts.words: One naturally interested in local affairs
parts.note: local here is a pub, the local, so its affairs are of concern to the person running it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub; its affairs concern the person who runs it, not a town councillor.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, which Britons call their local.

clue.text: He faces eight in a row

definitions.text: He faces eight in a row

parts.words: He faces eight in a row
parts.note: in a rowing eight, the steersman sits facing the eight rowers

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a row' sounds like a line, but it is rowing: in an eight the steersman faces the oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The person steering a racing boat sits in the stern facing the rowers.

clue.text: Society allows a girl to embrace a boy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the girl's name goes around the boy

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A permissive society lets a girl hug a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: MARY embraces SON; 'allows' joins the pieces. The Society is the Freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: The fraternal society of Freemasons is often called by this collective name.

clue.text: Profitable form of skating

definitions.note: the adjective stands for what is profitable, the money taken in

indicators.note: a new form of the word skating is its letters arranged differently

explanation.walkthrough: SKATING rearranges, signalled by 'form of', into the money a business takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the receipts, the profitable cash a shop or show brings in.

clue.text: Cyril burst into song

indicators.note: burst suggests something broken apart, so the letters of the name Cyril are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A man named Cyril starts singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into song' is a phrase, but 'burst' is the anagram signal on CYRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is the words of a song, or a short song-like poem.

clue.text: A show to be seen again ?

definitions.text: A show to be seen again ?

parts.words: A show to be seen again ?
parts.note: a stage entertainment whose French-derived name means looked at once more

explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from French: 're' means again and 'vue' means seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a stage show of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: By this, victory may be won in the long run

definitions.text: By this, victory may be won in the long run

parts.words: By this, victory may be won in the long run
parts.note: a narrow margin in a horse race, a small fraction of a horse's length

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' means eventually, but here it is a long race; a horse can win by the smallest margin.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the narrowest winning margin is less than a full length of the head.

clue.text: He takes pains not to feel them

definitions.text: He takes pains not to feel them

parts.words: He takes pains not to feel them
parts.note: a person who endures hardship without complaint, trying not to let suffering affect them

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes pains' means makes great effort, but here it also means bears pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the stoic outlook endures suffering with indifference.

clue.text: Met to construct a primitive symbol

indicators.note: to construct is to build, so the letters of met and to are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: People gathered to build an ancient emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: MET plus TO rearranges, signalled by 'construct'.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem, often a carved pole, venerated by a tribe or clan.

clue.text: This by itself is gross

parts.note: gross is the number 144, and twelve multiplied by twelve gives that

explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' means disgusting, but it is also 144, which is twelve times twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve of something make one batch, and twelve such batches make a gross.

clue.text: Apparently it's no good looking forward to an increment

definitions.text: Apparently it's no good looking forward to an increment

parts.words: Apparently it's no good looking forward to an increment
parts.note: an increment is a pay rise, and the word read as two parts says not at any time additional

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NEVER MORE, the answer says no increase will ever come; it is also the raven's refrain in Poe's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at no future time, so hoping for an increase is hopeless.

clue.text: First, first and last literally it's a gem

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class
literally, the first letter of the alphabet is A
literally, the last letter of the alphabet is Z

explanation.surface: A jewel judged first, the best of the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' says the second 'first' and the 'last' are letters: A and Z, the alphabet's first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, typically yellow.

clue.text: Half of them come to the conclusion it's correct

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its back two letters here

parts.note: the conclusion is the end

explanation.surface: Some of them reach a decision that it's right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of them' gives the back half of THEM, EM; 'come to' joins it to END.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing errors.

clue.text: Should this craft carry a log-book?

definitions.text: Should this craft carry a log-book?

parts.words: Should this craft carry a log-book?
parts.note: a vessel whose name comes from Tamil for tied logs, so it was itself made of logs

explanation.walkthrough: Every ship carries a log-book, but this craft takes its name from the Tamil for tied logs.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled boat descends from Tamil rafts of logs lashed together.
